15.stem_plain: The shopkeeper ________ the customer's request for an exchange as the product was defective.

15.zh: 由于产品有缺陷，店主同意了顾客的退换货要求。
15.note: “acceded to”意为“同意（某人的请求/要求）”。因为商品有缺陷（defective），店主答应顾客退换货（request for an exchange）的做法合情合理，搭配最为贴切。
15.concept: 动词短语搭配 Phrasal Verbs

choices.zh: 同意，应允（指在他人请求或要求后表示同意或准许，多用于正式场合）
choices.eg: The government finally acceded to the public demands for tax reform.

choices.zh: 让步，承认（指不情愿地承认某事属实或在辩论、斗争中让步）
choices.eg: He was forced to concede to his opponent after losing the major argument.

choices.zh: 继续进行（指在停顿或做完一件事后，开始或继续进行下一项活动）
choices.eg: After answering a few questions, the lecturer proceeded with the lesson.

choices.zh: 在……方面取得成功（指在某项 activity 中获得了预期的成功结果）
choices.eg: The team succeeded with their new marketing strategy, boosting sales.

cloze: Marconi was not just a pet dog. He was a professional guide dog that had learnt to lead an elderly blind woman. When she [Q51], he was returned to the organisation that had [Q52] him as a guide dog. Although he was not yet five years old, he was considered too [Q53] to be matched with another blind person. That was how I ended up adopting him.

As the new [Q54] of Marconi, I learnt that he was not [Q55] other dogs. He did not know how to play. He was used to being constantly on [Q56] and retirement puzzled him. He was [Q57] more than a metre from either myself or my husband, John.

Marconi watched our every movement. One evening, John and I were watching television while Marconi was watching us. John [Q58] and started for the kitchen. I was seated on the couch. Marconi leaped up and then stood frozen in his [Q59] between us. His head swivelled [Q60] one to the other of us. He moved two steps [Q61] John, stopped, retreated a step in my [Q62] and stopped again. He was filled with uncertainty, starting and stopping. Who needed him more? Eventually, he learnt to adjust living with [Q63].

Still, we were awed by Marconi's self-control. He was always disciplined. Yet, one day, I did find a mess downstairs. I reached for Marconi to reprimand him. But for [Q64], he wanted some distance between us. Eluding me, he loped upstairs to his den and chose his own [Q65]. He made himself stand in the corner.
zh: 马可尼不仅仅是一只宠物狗。他是一只专业的导盲犬，曾学会引导一位失明的老妇人。当她去世时，他被送回了曾将他训练为导盲犬的机构。虽然他还不满五岁，但他被认为年纪太大了，无法再与其他盲人进行配对。这就是我最终收养他的原因。
作为马可尼的新主人，我了解到他与其他狗不同。他不知道该怎么玩耍。他习惯了时刻处于执勤状态，退役让他感到困惑。他离我和我丈夫约翰的距离从来不会超过一米。
马可尼注视着我们的一举一动。一天晚上，约翰和我正在看电视，而马可尼在看着我们。约翰站起身，朝厨房走去。我坐在沙发上。马可尼跳了起来，然后僵立在原地，停在两人的中间。他的头在我们两个人之间转来转去。他朝约翰走了两步，停了下来，又朝我的方向退了一步，然后再次停下。他内心充满了不确定性，走走停停。谁更需要他？最终，他学会了适应与我们一起生活。
尽管如此，马可尼的自我克制依然让我们惊叹。他总是非常守纪律。然而有一天，我确实在楼下发现了一团糟。我伸手去抓马可尼想要训斥他。但仅此一次，他希望和我们保持一定的距离。他避开我，慢跑着上楼去了他自己的小窝，并选择了属于他自己的惩罚（或角落）。他让自己在角落里罚站。

51.note:
1. 上下文线索：前句提到这只导盲犬曾为一位失明的老妇人领路，后句指出它“被送回了机构”，由此可推断出老妇人“去世”或“不能继续抚养”。
  2. 语法要点：when 引导的时间状语从句，叙述过去发生的事实，需使用一般过去时（died 或 passed away）。

52.concept: 过去完成时与动词搭配
52.note:
1. 上下文线索：该机构原本就是专门管理导盲犬的（as a guide dog），所以是最初“训练”或“抚养”它的地方。
  2. 语法要点：定语从句中 had 后面需要接过去分词（trained），构成过去完成时，表示在被老妇人领养之前就已经完成的动作。

53.note:
1. 上下文线索：后文提到“这就是我最终收养它的原因”，说明由于某种限制它无法再与盲人匹配。前面提到它“还不满五岁”，对于高强度工作的导盲犬来说这个年龄已经被视为偏大。
  2. 语法要点：固定搭配 too + 形容词 + to do something，表示“太……以至于不能……”。

54.note:
1. 上下文线索：第一段末尾说“I ended up adopting him（我最终收养了他）”，所以此处指“作为它的新主人”。
  2. 语法要点：修饰人和动物的关系，使用 owner（所有人）或 master（主人）。

55.note:
1. 上下文线索：后句紧接着解释它“不知道该怎么玩耍，总是处于工作状态”，这些都属于不同于普通宠物狗的特征。
  2. 语法要点：be not like... 意为“不像……”，此处 like 作介词。

56.note:
1. 上下文线索：马可尼之前是一只专业的导盲犬，习惯了时刻处于紧绷、执勤的状态。
  2. 语法要点：固定短语 on duty（值班、执勤）、on guard（警惕、看守）或 on alert（警戒）。

57.note:
1. 上下文线索：前文强调它保持着时刻执勤的习惯，形影不离地关注着主人。所以它离开主人的距离“绝不会”或“很少”超过一米。
  2. 语法要点：结合句意填入否定副词，修饰整个句子的频度。

58.note:
1. 上下文线索：约翰和妻子本来在看电视，后面提到“started for the kitchen（走向厨房）”，因此前面发生的动作是“站起身”。
  2. 语法要点：整篇故事使用过去时，stood up（站起）或 got up（起来）在并列句中省去了 up，直接接动词过去式。

59.note:
1. 上下文线索：马可尼跳起来后就僵立在两个主人中间（stood frozen... between us）。
  2. 语法要点：英语固定词组 freeze/stop dead in one's tracks，意为“（因惊吓或困惑）突然原地僵住”。

60.note:
1. 上下文线索：它的头在两个主人之间转来转去，不知道该跟随着谁。
  2. 语法要点：与后文的 to 呼应，组成 from one to the other（从一个到另一个）。

61.note:
1. 上下文线索：后面提到“朝我的方向退了一步”，对比来看，前面它移动两步的目标是走向厨房的约翰。
  2. 语法要点：表示“朝向某人/某地移动”用介词 towards 或 toward。

62.note:
1. 上下文线索：在约翰和妻子之间纠结，朝约翰走两步后，又退回妻子这边。
  2. 语法要点：固定搭配 in one's direction（朝某人的方向）。

63.note:
1. 上下文线索：通过上文走走停停的纠结，它最终学会了适应与新家庭（也就是“我们”两个人）共同生活。
  2. 语法要点：介词 with 后接宾格代词 us，或泛指名词 humans。

64.note:
1. 上下文线索：本段开头强调它平时总是非常守纪律（always disciplined），但唯独今天搞砸了，并且想要躲避训斥。
  2. 语法要点：固定习语 but for once，表示“但仅此一次/唯独这一次（反常）”。

65.note:
1. 上下文线索：最后一句明确写道：“He made himself stand in the corner.”，直接给出了它去二楼后选择的去处和行为。
  2. 语法要点：与后句的名词进行同词重现（corner），或者归纳其行为本质为自我“惩罚”（punishment）。

67.stem_plain: John must see a doctor. He will not be able to get well soon.

66.stem_plain: None of the students refused to attend the holiday camp.

68.stem_plain: I tried very hard to assure my mother but she was still upset.

69.stem_plain: She did not know that there was a stranger lurking nearby.

70.stem_plain: Peter likes to sing. He does not like any other activities.

67.concept: 条件状语从句 — unless (if not)
67.zh: 除非看医生，否则约翰不会很快痊愈。
67.note: 连词用法：unless 引导条件状语从句，主句用一般将来时，从句用一般现在时（主将从现）。
67.answer: John will not be able to get well soon unless he sees a doctor.

66.concept: 双重否定变肯定 — Double Negative to Positive
66.zh: 所有的学生都参加了假期训练营。
66.note: 句型转换：双重否定 None ... refused to attend 转换为肯定句 All ... attended（或 agreed to attend）。
66.answer: All the students attended the holiday camp.

68.concept: 让步状语从句 — No matter how + adjective/adverb
68.zh: 无论我多么努力地安慰我母亲，她仍然很难过。
68.note: 句型结构：No matter how + 副词 (hard) + 主谓，逗号后连接主句，注意去掉原句中的连词 but。
68.answer: No matter how hard I tried to assure my mother, she was still upset.

69.concept: 固定形容词短语作状语 — Unknown to someone
69.zh: 她不知道附近有一个陌生人在潜伏。
69.note: 词组转换：动词短语 She did not know 转换为前置状语 Unknown to her（对她而言是未知的）。
69.answer: Unknown to her, there was a stranger lurking nearby.

70.zh: 除了唱歌，彼得不喜欢任何其他活动。
70.note: 排除介词：except 后面需要接名词、代词或动名词。此处将动词短语 to sing 转化为动名词 singing，并精简句子结构。
70.answer: Peter does not like any activities except singing.

76.stem_plain: Which word in paragraph 3 means "not intentionally"?

77.stem_plain: Explain why Keong was able to charge at Wayne without getting hurt.

80.stem_plain: Do you agree that Joey should never have listened to Wayne? Give one reason for your answer.

72.stem_plain: Why were they at the store?

"There was a collective gasp from the people as they shuddered at what might happen to them next." (Line 8 & 9)
Explain clearly what the people were afraid might happen to them next.

lines.1: Wayne paced around thinking what to do next. "You are wearing out the carpet," Joey
lines.2: told his friend. "Just stay calm and we will figure out a solution." Wayne did not reply,
lines.3: deep in thought over the predicament they were in. He glanced at the clock on the
lines.4: wall. It had been an hour since their ordeal began and they had run out of options.
lines.5: After several minutes of silence, Wayne finally spoke, "We've got to make a run for
lines.6: it with the loot. That's our only choice. We'll take two of them along with us." He
lines.7: waved his revolver at the group of people huddled at one corner of the room. There
lines.8: was a collective gasp from the people as they shuddered at what might happen to them
lines.9: next. Joey did not share Wayne's assessment. "Are you serious? The store is
lines.10: completely surrounded by the police. We do not stand a chance once we leave the
lines.11: store," he said, the fear all too evident in his voice.
lines.12: Joey stood up slowly, wiping the sweat from his forehead. He glared at Wayne with a
lines.13: look of anxiety mixed with resentment. He knew he should not have gone along with
lines.14: his accomplice's plan. "I should never have listened to you. Look at the mess it has
lines.15: landed us in." Joey's fear had transformed into anger as he grabbed Wayne by the
lines.16: collar with one hand. Taken aback by the sudden aggression, Wayne pushed him away
lines.17: instinctively. Joey stumbled, lost his balance and fell backwards. There was a loud
lines.18: thud as his head hit the cashier's counter. As Joey's lifeless body slumped to the floor,
lines.19: the rifle he had been holding went off without warning. The trigger had inadvertently
lines.20: been pulled when he lost grip of it.
lines.21: A few of the hostages screamed when the shot rang out. Wayne was momentarily
lines.22: stunned as the bullet had missed him only by a few inches and lodged itself in the wall
lines.23: behind him. Sensing that this was the opportunity he needed, Keong, the store
lines.24: assistant sprang to his feet and charged headlong into Wayne. The impact flung both
lines.25: men into the tables that had been stacked against the door by the gunmen. Wayne
lines.26: recovered more quickly and immediately threw a punch. Keong was hit squarely on
lines.27: the jaw and was knocked unconscious.
lines.28: Emboldened by Keong's actions, the other hostages moved towards Wayne. Sensing
lines.29: this, Wayne scrambled for his revolver which lay just beside him. Having retrieved it,
lines.30: he pointed it at them and threatened, "Don't come any closer or you will get it." The
lines.31: hostages immediately froze, realising the consequence if they moved a step closer.
lines.32: "Put that down!" a voice hollered behind Wayne. Shocked, he slowly turned round to
lines.33: see several officers pointing their weapons at him. He knew that the game was up. He
lines.34: had not noticed that the police had broken through the barricade during his struggle

paragraphs.1: 韦恩来回走动，思考下一步该做什么。“你在磨损地毯，”乔伊对他的朋友说。“冷静点，我们会找到解决办法的。”韦恩没有回答，陷入对他们所处困境的沉思。他看了一眼墙上的钟。自他们的苦难开始以来已经过去了一个小时，他们已经无路可走。
paragraphs.5: 沉默了几分钟后，韦恩终于开口了：“我们必须带着赃物逃跑。那是我们唯一的选择。我们会带他们中的两个人一起走。”他对着蜷缩在房间角落的一群人挥舞着他的左轮手枪。人们集体倒吸了一口凉气，一想到接下来会发生什么就浑身发抖。乔伊并不同意韦恩的评估。“你是认真的吗？商店完全被警察包围了。一旦我们离开商店，我们就没有半点机会，”他说，声音里满是恐惧。
paragraphs.12: 乔伊慢慢站起身，擦了擦额头上的汗。他瞪着韦恩，眼神里充满了焦虑与怨恨。他知道自己不该盲从这个同伙的计划。“我真不该听你的。看看这把我们带入了怎样的烂摊子。”乔伊的恐惧转化为了愤怒，他用一只手揪住了韦恩的衣领。韦恩被这突如其来的侵犯吓了一跳，本能地推开了他。乔伊踉跄了一下，失去了平衡摔倒在地上。发出一声沉重的闷响，他的头撞在了收银台上。当乔伊毫无生气的身体瘫倒在地上时，他一直拿着的步枪毫无预警地走火了。当他松开手时，扳机被无意中扣动了。
paragraphs.21: 枪声响起时，几名人质尖叫起来。韦恩瞬间惊呆了，因为子弹只差几英寸就打中了他，并卡在身后的墙里。意识到这是他需要的机会，店员阿强（Keong）一跃而起，迎头冲向韦恩。撞击力将两人推向枪手堆放在门前的桌子上。韦恩恢复得更快，随即挥出一拳。阿强下巴结结实实挨了一拳，被打晕了过去。
paragraphs.28: 受到阿强行动的鼓舞，其他人质向韦恩围了过来。察觉到这一点，韦恩急忙去拿掉在身旁的左轮手枪。拿回枪后，他指着他们威胁道：“别再靠近，否则有你们好看的。”人质们立刻僵住了，意识到如果再往前走一步的后果。
paragraphs.32: “把枪放下！”韦恩身后传来一声大喝。他大吃一惊，缓缓转过身，看到几名警察正用武器指着他。他知道大势已去。他没有注意到警察在自己与阿强搏斗期间已经突破了路障。

71.note:
1. 题型：指代题。
  2. 分析：结合前文，第1行明确提到“Wayne paced around... Joey told his friend”，随后第2行说明他们正在寻找解决方案。因此，第4行的“they”指代的就是这两个人。
  3. 得分点：必须完整写出 Wayne 和 Joey 两人，漏掉任何一人均不得分。

73.note:
1. 题型：名词指代题。
  2. 分析：第7行提到这群人蜷缩在房间角落，随后在第21行和第28行中，这些人被明确称为“hostages（人质）”。
  3. 得分点：关键词为“hostages（人质）”。

75.note:
1. 题型：细节理解题。
  2. 分析：根据第9-11行，乔伊说“The store is completely surrounded by the police. We do not stand a chance once we leave the store”，表明他害怕一旦离开就会落入法网。
  3. 得分点：指出“被警察逮捕/完全没有逃脱机会”。
75.answer: He feared that they would be caught or shot by the police, as the store was completely surrounded.

76.note:
1. 题型：词汇替换题。
  2. 分析：第三段第19-20行提到“The trigger had inadvertently been pulled when he lost grip of it.”，这里的“inadvertently”与“not intentionally（非故意地、不经意地）”意思完全吻合。
  3. 得分点：必须准确拼写出单个词汇“inadvertently”，多写或错拼不得分。

77.note:
1. 题型：因果细节分析题（2分）。
  2. 分析：第21-24行指出，枪声响后，子弹擦过韦恩，韦恩“momentarily stunned（瞬间惊呆了）”。店员阿强正是敏锐地“Sensing that this was the opportunity he needed”才冲上去的。
  3. 得分点：1分指出“枪声突然响起且子弹差点打中韦恩”；1分指出“韦恩处于极度震惊/分神的状态，无法及时反应”。
77.answer: Keong took advantage of the moment when Wayne was momentarily stunned by the sudden rifle gunshot that had just missed him.

80.note:
1. 题型：观点阐述题（2分）。
  2. 分析：此题为开放性问题，但须结合文本逻辑。根据第14-18行，乔伊自己也极其后悔（Look at the mess it has landed us in），且最终因为内讧摔倒在收银台，身体“lifeless（失去生气）”。
  3. 得分点：1分明确表达观点（如 Yes/I agree）；1分给出基于文本的合理原因（如：该计划导致他违法犯罪、陷入绝境，甚至最终丧命）。
80.answer: Yes, I agree. Listening to Wayne's plan led Joey into a dangerous crime scene, trapped by the police, and ultimately caused his accidental head injury and death.

72.note:
1. 题型：事实细节题。
  2. 分析：根据第6行提到的“make a run for it with the loot（带着赃物逃跑）”以及第25行提到的“gunmen（枪手）”，可以推断出他们来到这家商店是为了实施抢劫。
  3. 得分点：准确表达出“抢劫”或“盗取财物”的意图即可。
72.answer: They were there to commit a robbery / steal items.

74.note:
1. 题型：心理分析题（2分）。
  2. 分析：在人质倒吸凉气之前，韦恩刚刚说“We'll take two of them along with us（我们会带他们中的两个人一起走）”并挥舞着左轮手枪。因此，人们害怕的是被当作人质带走，并面临生命危险。
  3. 得分点：1分扣住“被带走作为逃跑的挡箭牌/人质”；1分扣住“受到枪支威胁/受到身体伤害”。
74.answer: They were afraid that they would be taken along by Wayne and Joey as they made a run for it, and that they might be harmed or killed by Wayne's revolver.

78.note:
1. 题型：行为目的题。
  2. 分析：第25行提到桌子被“stacked against the door by the gunmen”，而在结尾第34行提到“the police had broken through the barricade”，这说明堆放桌子是为了建立路障，阻挡警察。
  3. 得分点：提到“阻挡警察”或“防止外面的人进入”。
78.answer: To barricade the entrance and prevent the police from entering the store easily.

79.note:
1. 题型：虚拟结果推断题。
  2. 分析：第30行韦恩恶狠狠地威胁道：“Don't come any closer or you will get it.”，这里的“get it”在枪支威胁的语境下，意思就是会被子弹射中。
  3. 得分点：必须指出“会被韦恩开枪射击”这一严重后果。
79.answer: Wayne would have shot them with his revolver.

sample: My name is Jie and I am from class Primary 6B. I am writing **on behalf of** my class to **seek your permission** to hold a performance for our teachers on 29 October 2021.

--As-- my classmates and I will be **posted to** our secondary schools in just three months, we would like to do something special for all our teachers to **show our appreciation** for what they have done for us over the last six years.
markdown: 这个关于向校长申请举办感恩表演的正式信函（Situational Writing）是一篇非常标准且展现了极高语言素养的 PSLE 实用文体高分范文。主要亮点如下：

### 1. 任务全面达标 (Complete Task Fulfillment)
* **完美覆盖所有要点**：
  * **写信目的与日期**：第一段开门见山，代表全班申请在2021年10月29日举办表演（“seek your permission... on 29 October 2021”）。
  * **举办表演的原因**：三个月后就要毕业并分派到中学，想表达对老师六年教导的感恩（“show our appreciation... over the last six years”）。
  * **表演人员与形式**：由作者（Jie）、Siti和Dev共同创作一首专门献给老师的歌，并由全班同学一起演唱（“sing it with the rest of our class”）。
  * **两个其他细节**：细节①是这是一首专为老师创作的歌曲；细节②是希望全校保密，以便给老师们制造一个惊喜（“keep the plan under wraps”）。

### 2. 完美遵从正式公文的格式与礼仪 (Perfect Formal Register & Tone)
* **称呼与结语极为得体**：邮件开头使用了正式的 `"Dear Mr Sim,"`，结尾使用了尊重的 `"Yours sincerely,"` 配合全名 `"Jie Wong"`，完全符合写给校长的标准行政书信格式。
* **语气极具修养**：整封信充满了恳切与尊重。在提出请求时使用了 `"seek your permission"`（寻求您的批准），在表达渴望时使用了高级委婉的语气助词 `"we would like to"` 和 `"we would really appreciate it if..."`，非常得体。

### 3. 精准使用高级地道习语与固定搭配 (Advanced Vocabulary & Idioms)
* 文章的词汇密度和地道程度非常抢眼：
  * 用 `"on behalf of"` 精准表达“代表全班”；
  * 用 `"dedicated to"` 表达这首歌是“专门献给”老师的；
  * 最出彩的是使用了地道高级习语 `"keep the plan under wraps"`（对计划进行保密），这让文章的语言质感直接拔高到了 AL1 的顶尖水平。

### 4. 逻辑顺畅，首尾呼应 (Smooth Transitions & Professional Closing)
* 段落之间过渡自然。使用 `--As--` 引出背景原因（因为即将毕业、因为想保留惊喜），使得每一个请求都师出有名。
* 结尾段使用经典的商务/行政书信结语 `"favourable response"`（令人满意的答复），展现了极强的应用文写作功底。
